conventions.evidence: Follows sibling style (typed private const, private helper, PHPDoc on class and helper), ships tests, updates .env.example, docs/ops/devops.md and docs/ops/logging.md. However conventions.md 'Keep docs in sync' also requires a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased], and the diff has none.

security.evidence: Strict allow-list with anchored \A...\z regex after trim (DiscordOpsAlert.php:31,96-100); non-string/non-int values rejected (:93-95); @everyone/@here/newline injection cases cannot pass. Existing redaction and webhook-URL-free logging untouched.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:125-227 cover exact mention format, int and trimmed input, null/''/whitespace, a broad invalid dataset ('@everyone', '@here', 'abc', '123', 16 and 21 digits, "123\n@everyone", "123> \n@everyone", negative, embedded '<@'), and truncation keeping the mention at exactly 1800 chars. Missing a valid 20-digit upper-bound case; the no-mention 1800-char case relies on existing tests not shown in the diff.

simplicity.evidence: One small private mention() helper plus a two-line change in formatContent (DiscordOpsAlert.php:74-79); reuses the existing MaxContentLength and content-building code; no new classes or layers.

readability.evidence: Clear names (mention(), MentionIdPattern), a short comment explaining the reservation (:76), a PHPDoc on the helper describing its return value (:82-84); no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every touched file (.env.example, DiscordOpsAlert.php, config/services.php, two ops docs, the test file) serves the task; no unrelated edits.

issues.explanation: conventions.md requires a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] for changes, and the new DISCORD_MENTION_ID feature isn't recorded there.
The valid-ID tests only use 17-digit IDs; a 20-digit valid case would pin down the upper bound of the {17,20} range.

review.summary: The change adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID config. A strictly anchored 17-20 digit allow-list validates it, and the mention is appended on its own line with room reserved inside the 1800-character cap. Tests cover valid, empty, malicious and truncation cases, and the env/ops docs are updated. The change is correct, secure and lean, so it can be approved with nits: it lacks a CHANGELOG entry and a test for a 20-digit ID.
